tldr: The paper introduces INTERS, a novel instruction tuning dataset of 200k examples spanning 20 tasks across 43 datasets, designed to significantly improve LLMs' performance on information retrieval tasks through supervised fine-tuning.
contributions: INTERS dataset with 20 tasks across three IR categories (query understanding, document understanding, query-document relationship understanding) derived from 43 distinct datasets
Manually crafted 12 unique templates per dataset plus detailed task descriptions
Comprehensive evaluation showing INTERS consistently boosts performance of LLaMA, Mistral, and Falcon models
Ablation studies on instruction design, template diversity, few-shot demonstrations, data volume, and ranking strategies
methods: The authors constructed INTERS by collecting 43 publicly available IR datasets covering 20 tasks, then manually crafted 12 natural-language templates per dataset (including inverse templates), wrote detailed task descriptions, and generated zero-shot to five-shot examples filtered at 2,048 tokens. They compiled 200k examples using an examples-proportional mixing strategy capped at 5k per dataset. Four open-source LLMs (Falcon-RW-1B, Minima-2-3B, Mistral-7B, LLaMA-2-7B) were fine-tuned on INTERS and evaluated in-domain and out-of-domain across query understanding, document understanding, and query-document relationship understanding tasks.
results: INTERS fine-tuning consistently improved all models across IR tasks compared to untuned baselines. Average performance increased from 13.18 (No FT) to 46.42 (INTERS) across task categories. Category-level ablation showed query understanding, document understanding, and query-document relationship understanding are complementary (removing any category reduced performance). Task-level generalization was observed: models fine-tuned without query intent classification still outperformed untuned models on that task. Dataset-level generalization showed strong zero-shot transfer to unseen datasets. Custom templates and task descriptions significantly improved performance over no-template/no-description variants.
limitations: INTERS-Falcon performed worse than untuned Falcon on query-document relationship understanding tasks, attributed to the complexity of these tasks. Larger models without fine-tuning could still outperform smaller fine-tuned models on some relationship tasks. The optimal combination of datasets for instruction tuning remains unclear, as removing XSum from training unexpectedly improved performance on MultiNews.
